title: Graceful multi-region streaming handover and dynamic circuit-throttling for hosted API edge
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement an active-active edge/gateway failover mechanism that preserves streaming sessions where possible, performs graded traffic attenuation when capacity is constrained, and leverages circuit-breaker states to protect downstream runtime pools while keeping hosted API SLOs within target.

Background: We currently rely on regional failover that is session-unaware for most streaming requests. That causes visible user disruptions for long-lived streaming sessions (chat streaming, function-call streams). We need a solution that: (1) prefers non-disruptive, session-preserving handoffs when safe, (2) falls back to graceful short-live interruption with clear telemetry and recovery, and (3) enforces SLO-first shedding via dynamic circuit thresholds.

High-level approach: 
- Introduce a Stream Handoff Coordinator (SHC) at edge that tracks streaming session metadata (session ID, current sequence/token checkpoint, KV cache footprint estimate). SHC makes per-session routing decisions and coordinates token-stitching for short durations to rebind sessions to a new region instance.
- Implement a three-state circuit model (Green/Degraded/Tripped) per-region-per-model that feeds an attenuation controller. Green = route normally; Degraded = probabilistic fractional shedding and preferring local cache hits; Tripped = aggressive routing away and immediate fallback variants.
- Add graded traffic attenuation algorithm: attenuation fraction = f(SLO_headroom, inflight_queue_length, model_utilization, failover_penalty). This enables fine-grained shedding (e.g., 5%-50%) without full cutovers.
- Streaming considerations: for sessions with active KV caches or large prefix context, prefer short-lived proxy relay (ephemeral sticky relay) to avoid full KV rebuild on the target; relay holds a small in-flight window and performs checkpointing. For sessions that cannot be relayed (very long prefix or restricted data), allow ordered graceful termination with a structured error and automatic resume token for the client.

Non-goals: Full cross-region strong-consistency for customer KV data, changing client API semantics, or requiring client SDK upgrades (we may offer opt-in SDK hooks later).

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field below.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end handoff: A streaming session started in region A can be migrated to region B in staging without losing messages >95% of the time for sessions <6 minute duration under load.

SLO preservation: Under injected region failure tests, API p99 latency and error-rate SLOs degrade no worse than configured headroom targets (customer class dependent) when graded attenuation is enabled.
Circuit model: Regions expose Green/Degraded/Tripped events to metrics and to the Console. Triggering Tripped results in immediate routing fallback to reserved variants.
Observability: Console shows per-session handoff traces, attenuation fraction over time, and per-region circuit state with links to relevant logs and replay artifacts.
Rollback safe: Feature can be toggled via a console flag per-organization and reverted without orphaned relays or leaking KV checkpoints.
Load tests: Synthetic workload with 10k concurrent streaming sessions exercises the path and the system maintains target SLOs in >=90% of runs when configured headroom is 20%.
design_decision_summary: We chose a coordinator-and-relay hybrid: lightweight coordinator for decisioning + ephemeral relay for stateful sessions. This avoids full KV syncs for short migrations and prevents wholesale client-visible disconnects. Fractional attenuation allows incremental shedding aligned with SLO headroom rather than binary cutovers. Circuit states are coarse (3 states) to reduce flapping and simplify runbook actions.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Spike/staging): Implement SHC prototype and ephemeral relay; validate with synthetic streams and KV size emulation (completed 2026-03-11).
Phase 1 (Canary): Enable for 5% of traffic in us-west1→us-east1 for internal orgs; observe for 2 days and iterate (target 2026-03-18).
Phase 2 (Pilot): Expand to PLG customers with non-critical orgs in two regions; collect telemetry and incident runbooks (target 2026-03-25).
Phase 3 (GA): Gradual rollout to all hosted; default attenuation enabled with conservative thresholds and opt-out per-org (target 2026-04-01).
telemetry_requirements: Per-region circuit state events (Green/Degraded/Tripped) with timestamps and room for annotations.
Per-session handoff trace including timestamps for decision, relay start/stop, token-stitch events, and final outcome.
Attenuation fraction sampled at 10s granularity and correlated with model_utilization, headroom, and inflight_queue_length.
SLO rolling windows (1m,5m,1h) for latency and error rate, with headroom calculation visible to the attenuation controller.
Synthetic canary dashboards and automated alerts on handoff failure rate, relay orphaning, and unexpected p99 spikes.
test_plan: Unit tests for coordinator decision logic and attenuation formula with mocked telemetry inputs.
Integration tests: end-to-end streaming handoff with ephemeral relay and token rebind; simulated region drain and failover.
Chaos tests: induce partial region degradation (disk I/O penalty, increased RPC tail latency) and validate circuit transitions and shedding behavior.
Load test: 10k concurrent streams with mixed short/long sessions to validate KV-relay performance and no memory leaks.
Security test: ensure relay does not expose cross-tenant data; run static analysis and a short threat-model review.
